newsitem.title: UK: British Energy job cuts on safety watch.
newsitem.headline: British Energy job cuts on safety watch.

text.p: Britain's Nuclear Installations Inspectorate (NII) will review job cut plans by nuclear generator British Energy and will block them if there are any adverse effects on safety, a spokesman for NII said.
"If we think they are adverse, we will use regulatory powers to stop (British Energy) doing them," the spokesman said.
British Energy plans to cut 1,460 of its workforce, which totals over 6,500, in a bid to make staff cost savings of 50 million stg a year within three years.
The NII has not seen the company's detailed proposals yet and will wait for these before deciding on action.
The spokesman said British Energy must consult with NII before implementing job cuts but he could not say how long the process would take.
Unions were quick to criticise the plans, calling them "a high risk strategy," and warning the job cuts could "reduce training, lower standards and threaten safety."

A statement from representatives of unions at British Energy said that "by reducing technical support, and the number of skilled personnel running these stations, the company may be unable to run these stations safely."
